opus55-max.headline: C++ interior-point method that factors scenario blocks in SIMD batches and couples them through a Schur complement on the 121 linking columns.
structure: Finds the 121 linking columns from column counts; removing them splits the rows into scenario blocks
Two-level dense Schur complement: linking columns, then the 185 first-stage rows
Same-pattern blocks share one symbolic analysis and are factored four at a time in AVX2 lanes
opus55-max.approach: Mehrotra predictor-corrector with one Gondzio corrector on per-block normal equations (CAMD ordering, sparse Cholesky with dense tails). Most late gains came from memory traffic: fused vector passes and prefaulted heap pages.
opus55-max.fallback: A flop model picks the column-count threshold and union-find finds the blocks, so row and column order do not matter. With no linking columns it falls back to a single-block sparse IPM, which is why the split-variable OOD instance timed out.
log: First block-structured IPM with a linking-column Schur complement
Dense kernels for each block's linking tail halve factor time
Four same-pattern blocks batched per AVX2 lane group
Geometric scaling; threads capped at physical cores
Centering and neighbourhood tuning: 245 → 190 total iterations
Heap prefault; page faults had cost 10–17% per solve
Persistent zero vectors in correctors; selected
deadends: Dynamic OpenMP scheduling: 2.2× slower
Batch width 8: register pressure slowed factorization

astra-high.headline: C++ interior-point method that keeps dense columns as explicit unknowns and factors scenario components in parallel around a dense Schur system.
structure: The 121 columns with more than 32 nonzeros stay explicit in an augmented system (s100 factor time 16.7 s → 2.1 s)
Connected row components (the scenarios) factored in parallel with SuiteSparse LDL
Union-find presolve removes proportional and forced-zero variables (~14% of rows)
astra-high.approach: Mehrotra predictor-corrector with Ruiz scaling and a projected-gradient warm start, a dense LAPACK Schur complement over the connecting columns, and runtime-dispatched AVX-512/AVX2 kernels.
astra-high.fallback: A fixed column-count threshold and connected components make no ordering assumptions. It handled both STORM OOD shifts, falling back to plain CHOLMOD normal equations or a sparse augmented LDL when needed.
log: CHOLMOD normal-equation IPM; dense columns make factorization 92% of time

structure: Column domination: drop x_j when c_j exceeds the summed cheapest other covers of its rows
Dense normal equations over only 2,000–2,500 rows, factored in float, then double

opus55-max.fallback: Covering reductions are applied only to 0/1 matrices with ≥ rows and nonnegative costs. Anything else goes to a general bounded IPM. It stayed ahead of MOSEK on the real rail instances.

astra-high.fallback: The covering tricks need nonnegative covering rows and costs. Otherwise it runs a plain IPM. On the degenerate rail instances, CG solves before the working set took over cost 41 of 47 s, which made it 5× slower than MOSEK.

opus55-max.headline: Interior-point method that eliminates the n² link rows in closed form and solves a restricted master of cheap assignments, certified by pricing.
structure: Link rows grouped by y_j: each block is diagonal + rank one, eliminated by a stable rank-one LDLᵀ update
Dense Schur complement on only the n + 1 assignment and cardinality rows

opus55-max.fallback: Two-entry rows are detected as links with no ordering assumption, so general LPs run through the same IPM. Sifting runs only when a cardinality row exists, and a native full-LP solve and a numpy path back it up.

opus55-max.headline: GPU interior-point method in CuPy that reduces each Newton system to a dense customers × customers Schur complement.
structure: Link rows folded into a diagonal block, so assignment columns are eliminated in closed form
Capacity rows form a diagonal block of the Schur system and are eliminated before Cholesky

opus55-max.fallback: Rows and columns are classified by nonzero counts and incidence, so any LP runs through the same IPM with a larger dense block. On the 10,000-customer OOD instance that block had 10,100 rows and the solve took 49 s.

astra-high.headline: Native CUDA interior-point method that eliminates each facility block in closed form and factors a customer-sized Schur system in guarded mixed precision.
structure: Per-facility Hessian (diagonal + link arrow + rank-one capacity term) inverted analytically

astra-high.approach: CUDA C++ with cuBLAS/cuSOLVER, plus an ahead-of-time tiled Gram kernel that avoids cold cuBLAS compilation. A C++ parser recognizes the facility blocks in linear time.
astra-high.fallback: It validates the exact block pattern (strong or weak form) and otherwise falls back to a generic GPU PDHG. The aggregate-capacity OOD row broke the pattern, and the fallback hit its iteration limit.

opus55-max.headline: Hand-written CUDA restarted Halpern PDHG that detects the Adams–Johnson pattern and runs two specialized kernels on a dense facility-pair grid.
structure: y columns stored on a facility-pair grid so every gather is coalesced (2× faster per iteration)
Each y reduced cost reads its four linking duals contiguously from transposed copies

opus55-max.fallback: Detection validates every y column under any permutation. Other LPs go through a generic fused CSR/CSC PDHG with the same math, about 2× slower.

astra-high.headline: GPU Halpern PDHG on an exact symmetry quotient of the LP, found by color refinement, with FP32 corrections around an FP64 base.

astra-high.approach: A C++ library computes the coarsest equitable partition. CuPy kernels then run a reflected Halpern PDHG with restarts, a CG dual start, and degree-sorted ELL kernels in CUDA graphs.
astra-high.fallback: Nothing in it is QAP-specific: an LP without symmetry gets the identity quotient and the same PDHG. That is why the unstructured tai30a still took only 0.6 s, and why it solved every p-median instance in the cross-task probe.
